title: Why your press-on nails pop off in three days
meta_description: Press-ons lifting after a few days is almost always a prep problem, not a glue problem. The four minutes of prep that makes them last two to three weeks.
excerpt: Almost always prep, not glue. Four minutes of surface work is the difference between three days and three weeks.
intro: When a press-on lifts early, the instinct is to buy stronger glue. That is almost never the problem. Glue bonds to the nail plate — if anything is sitting between the two, it does not matter how strong it is, because it is bonding to that instead.

sections.heading: The real enemy is oil
paragraphs: Your nail plate produces natural oils continuously, and cuticle skin creeps over the base of the nail without you noticing. Both create a layer that glue cannot grip through.
This is why a set applied straight after a shower fails fastest — the nail is soft, swollen with water, and coated in whatever was in your body wash.

sections.heading: Sizing is the second failure
paragraphs: A press-on wider than your nail bed leaves the edges unsupported, and every knock levers it away from the nail. Choose the size that sits just inside your sidewalls rather than the one that covers everything.
If you are between sizes, take the smaller one and file your natural nail slightly, rather than forcing the larger.

sections.heading: Glue: thin, both sides, and press
paragraphs: A thick blob of glue does not cure properly in the middle and stays slightly soft, which is exactly what you do not want under a nail you are typing with.
A thin layer on the natural nail and a thin layer inside the press-on, then firm pressure for a full thirty seconds, outperforms a thick application every time.

steps.title: Push back the cuticles
steps.detail: Use a wooden stick or a rubber-ended pusher on dry nails. You are clearing the base of the nail plate, not cutting anything.
steps.tip: Do not cut your cuticles. That is your seal against infection.

steps.title: Buff the shine off
steps.detail: A few light passes with a fine buffer. The nail should look matte, not scratched. You are removing gloss, not thinning the nail.
steps.tip: Over-buffing thins the plate and causes long-term weakness. Light is enough.

steps.title: Dehydrate the surface
steps.detail: Wipe each nail with rubbing alcohol or a nail dehydrator and let it dry fully. This is the step that removes the oil.
steps.tip: Do not touch your nails after this. Skin oil transfers instantly.

steps.title: Size, glue thin, press 30 seconds
steps.detail: Match each nail before you start gluing. Thin layer on both surfaces, press from cuticle down, hold firmly and count to thirty.
steps.tip: Keep hands out of water for the next two hours while the bond finishes setting.

faqs.q: Is nail glue or adhesive tab better?
faqs.a: Tabs are gentler and removable but last a few days at most. Glue lasts one to three weeks. Tabs suit a one-night set; glue suits everyday wear.

faqs.q: How do I remove them without wrecking my nails?
faqs.a: Soak in warm soapy water or acetone until the bond softens, then lift gently. If it resists, soak longer. Prying them off takes layers of your natural nail with them.
Yes, if you remove them by soaking. Scrape the old glue off the inside before the next wear.
